# Adjudication Task — Chapter 42

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃42화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|게이트(Gate).
  6|
  7|대격변이 남긴 가장 큰 흔적.
  8|
  9|삼십여 년 전 마왕 아스모데우스가 침략 루트로 사용했던 그곳은, 헌터들의 생계 수단이자 마정석이라는 고차원 에너지 자원의 발굴 현장으로 전락한 지 오래였다.
 10|
 11|“평화 길드 분들이시죠?”
 12|
 13|입구에 나와 있던 작업복 차림의 중년인이 다가왔다.
 14|
 15|게이트마다 배치된 게이트 관리청 소속의 공무원이다.
 16|
 17|“네.”
 18|
 19|최 팀장의 무뚝뚝한 대답에 공무원이 고개를 끄덕였다.
 20|
 21|“딱 맞춰 오셨네요. 언제 진입하실 겁니까?”
 22|
 23|“장비 갖추고 바로 들어가겠습니다.”
 24|
 25|“2층에 대기실 있으니까 준비 마치고 내려오시면 됩니다. 그럼.”
 26|
 27|우리는 최 팀장을 따라 이동했다. 관리청 공무원이 상주하는 2층짜리 건물은 낡을 대로 낡았는데, 대기실 역시 비슷한 상황이었다.
 28|
 29|‘와 씨. 냄새 봐라.’
 30|
 31|문을 열자마자 땀 냄새가 코를 찌른다. 녹슨 캐비닛과 꽉 찬 휴지통도 눈에 띄었다.
 32|
 33|“여긴 좀 심하네. 환기도 안 시키나?”
 34|
 35|“게이트 담당 공무원들이 그렇지 뭐. 괜히 꿀 보직이 아니여.”
 36|
 37|나는 투덜거리는 소리를 뒤로하고 레이드 장비로 환복하기 시작했다. 가죽 갑옷에 가벼운 소재의 전투화. 마지막으로 길쭉한 케이스에서 창을 꺼내 쥐었다.
 38|
 39|‘오랜만이네.’
 40|
 41|손아귀에 딱 들어오는 이 감촉. 익숙하면서도 낯설다.
 42|
 43|지난 한 달 동안 썼던 무기와는 확실히 차이가…… 아, 아니다. 더는 생각하지 말자.
 44|
 45|‘이젠 다 잊어야지.’
 46|
 47|괜히 멀쩡한 전투화 끈을 조이는 내게 임꺽정이 다가왔다.
 48|
 49|그는 전신 갑옷과 거대한 타워 실드를 갖춘 메인 탱커의 모습이었다.
 50|
 51|“준비 끝났어?”
 52|
 53|“예. 뭐.”
 54|
 55|나를 위아래로 훑어본 임꺽정이 혀를 내둘렀다.
 56|
 57|“이 녀석 보게. 도대체 언제 적 장비야?”
 58|
 59|“글쎄요. 처음 시작할 때 샀으니까 적어도 7년?”
 60|
 61|초짜 시절, 동대문 지하 매장에서 큰맘 먹고 질렀더랬다. 가격도 정확히 기억한다. 198만 원.
 62|
 63|‘지르고 나서 며칠 동안 잠도 제대로 못 잤지.’
 64|
 65|헌터는 수입만큼 지출도 큰 직업이다. 그 지출의 대부분을 차지하는 게 장비 관련이고. 이게 다 게이트의 특수성 때문이다.
 66|
 67|‘마나, 혹은 마력이 깃들지 않은 장비는 금방 망가지니까.’
 68|
 69|그래서 가장 흔하게 쓰이는 방법이 게이트 몬스터에게 얻은 마정석을 재료로 장비를 제작하는 거다.
 70|
 71|사용된 마정석의 등급이 높을수록 가격은 천정부지로 솟는다.
 72|
 73|“7년? 세상에. 아무리 돈이 좋아도 쓸 때는 써야지. 목숨에 돈 아낄래?”
 74|
 75|“음. 사정이 있었어요.”
 76|
 77|굳이 말하고 싶지 않은 사정이다. 임꺽정은 걱정스러운 목소리로 말했다.
 78|
 79|“오늘은 비전투 포지션이니 괜찮겠지만…… 조심해라.”
 80|
 81|“네.”
 82|
 83|대답하면서도 기분이 묘하다. 얼마 전까지 조심하라는 말을 입에 달고 살던 누군가가 떠올라서.
 84|
 85|하지만 감상에 젖는 것도 잠시.
 86|
 87|“다들 준비 끝나셨습니까?”
 88|
 89|최 팀장의 등장에 나는 입을 딱 벌렸다.
 90|
 91|저거 설마.
 92|
 93|“붉은 드레이크 가죽 세트?”
 94|
 95|“음.”
 96|
 97|최 팀장의 얼굴이 굳었다. 명품관 카탈로그에서나 보던 거라 나도 모르게 그만 실수했다.
 98|
 99|“아, 죄송합…….”
100|
101|“별거 아닙니다. 다섯 종류의 마법과 B급 마정석을 재료로 만들었을 뿐이죠.”
102|
103|“……?”
104|
105|“강조하는 건 아니지만 다섯 종류의 마법과 B급 마정석이 재료입니다.”
106|
107|“아, 네.”
108|
109|“붉은 드레이크의 가죽이 인기가 좋은 건 특유의 윤기 때문인데, 보기에만 그럴듯하고 별 쓸모는 없습니다.”
110|
111|최 팀장이 굳은 얼굴로 몸을 움직였다. 은은한 붉은 빛이 번뜩였다.
112|
113|“하지만 매우 아름답죠.”
114|
115|“…….”
116|
117|“이만 내려갑시다.”
118|
119|최 팀장이 먼저 대기실을 나가자 임꺽정이 다가와 말했다.
120|
121|“저 친구 장비 알아봐 주는 거 엄청 좋아해.”
122|
123|“아니 뭐, 이해는 가는데…… 왜 저래요?”
124|
125|“몰라. 장비 덕후야. 전 재산 털어서 저거 사고 밤마다 입고 잔다는 소문도 있어.”
126|
127|저 자식도 또라이구나.
128|
129|나는 내심 한탄하며 오늘 레이드가 무사히 끝나길 빌었다.
130|
131|
132|
133|* * *
134|
135|
136|
137|“신청하신 인원이랑 다르군요.”
138|
139|공무원은 불편한 표정이었다. 그럴 만도 하지. 이제 진입해야 하는데 인원이 전부 안 모였으니까.
140|
141|‘도대체 얼마나 기다려야 하나.’
142|
143|현재 게이트 앞에 집결한 인원은 여섯 명. 짐꾼으로 온 나를 제외하면 전투 인원은 다섯밖에 안 된다.
144|
145|E급 게이트니까 최소한 동급의 헌터 다섯이 더 필요한데…… 평화 길드 놈들이 코빼기도 보이지 않으니 공무원 입장에서는 짜증이 날 수밖에.
146|
147|“추가된 인원이 있으면 미리 말씀을 해 주셔야죠.”
148|
149|응? 방금 뭐라고 한 거냐.
150|
151|추가된 인원이라니?
152|
153|“죄송합니다.”
154|
155|최 팀장의 무뚝뚝한 사과에 공무원이 펜을 들어 서류에 좍좍 줄을 그었다.
156|
157|“뭐 수정하면 되니까 큰 문제는 없는데…… 다음부턴 조심해 주십쇼.”
158|
159|“예.”
160|
161|큰 문제가 없기는 시발. 사람이 없잖아, 사람이!
162|
163|나는 임꺽정의 옆구리를 쿡 찔렀다.
164|
165|“형님. 다른 사람들은 언제 와요?”
166|
167|“무슨 사람들?”
168|
169|“평화 길드요.”
170|
171|“최 팀장 있잖아.”
172|
173|“네?”
174|
175|“아, 말 안 했었나? 평화 길드, 신생이라 인원이 없어. 길드장 포함 세 명이 전부지. 으하하.”
176|
177|……웃어?
178|
179|“아니, 형님.”
180|
181|“알아, 인마. 근데 걱정 안 해도 돼.”
182|
183|내 어깨를 툭 친 임꺽정이 서류에 사인 중인 최 팀장을 가리켰다.
184|
185|“저 양반, C급 헌터거든.”
186|
187|“아. C급…….”
188|
189|나는 입을 다물었다. 최 팀장이 C급 헌터라면 문제없다. 아니, E급 헌터 열 명보다 훨씬 낫다. 그는 나 같은 하급 헌터와 격이 다른 ‘중급 헌터’니까.
190|
191|‘명품 장비 걸쳤을 때부터 알아차렸어야 했는데.’
192|
193|고급 아파트를 몸에 두르고 다니는 인간이다. 어지간한 하급 헌터들은 전 재산을 열 번 털어도 못 사는 가격.
194|
195|최 팀장의 뒷모습에서 은은한 후광이 비쳤다.
196|
197|“서명 확인 바랍니다.”
198|
199|공무원에게 펜을 넘겨주는 모습도 어쩜 저렇게 우아하냐.
200|
201|작은 움직임조차 부티가 좔좔 흐르는 것 같다.
202|
203|저게 바로 C급 헌터의 품격인가.
204|
205|‘존나 멋있어.’
206|
207|의형제 맺고 싶다. 게이트 아래에서 게이결의, 아니 게이트결의 맺고 싶다.
208|
209|“자, 그럼 이제 들어갈…… 뭡니까?”
210|
211|최 팀장이 흠칫한 얼굴로 나를 바라봤다.
212|
213|“아뇨. 그냥 멋있어서요.”
214|
215|“네?”
216|
217|“장비. 멋있다고요.”
218|
219|그 순간, 최 팀장의 입꼬리가 꿈틀거렸다.
220|
221|“별거 아닙니다. 다섯 종류의 마법과 B급 마정석을 재료로…….”
222|
223|친해지고 싶은 또라이다.
224|
225|
226|
227|* * *
228|
229|
230|
231|게이트를 향해 한 걸음을 내디뎠다.
232|
233|쏴아악-
234|
235|익숙한 느낌이 전신을 감싼다. 서늘하면서 끈적거리는 마력 특유의 기운. 그리고 뒤바뀐 풍경.
236|
237|“동굴이군요.”
238|
239|최 팀장의 말처럼 이번 레이드 장소는 동굴이었다. 습기를 머금은 벽면은 축축했고 사방은 옅은 어둠에 잠겨 있었다.
240|
241|“태경 씨. 손전등 꺼내세요.”
242|
243|“넵.”
244|
245|나는 재빨리 배낭을 내려놨다. 게이트 진입 직전, 최 팀장에게 건네받은 짐꾼용 가방이다. 겉보기에는 평범하지만 무려 공간 확장에 경량화 마법까지 걸려 있는 고가의 물품.
246|
247|“여기 있습니다. 손전등.”
248|
249|달라니까 주긴 하는데, 내 경험상 그리 좋은 방법은 아니다. 간편한 대신 빛이 사라질 경우 갑작스러운 어둠에 적응하지 못하기 때문이다.
250|
251|차라리 잠깐 대기하면서 눈에 어둠이 익기를 기다리는 게 훨씬…….
252|
253|딸깍.
254|
255|“빛이 있으라. 라이트(Light).”
256|
257|슈웅. 손전등으로부터 축구공만 한 빛 덩어리가 튀어나와 동굴 천장에 철썩 달라붙는다.
258|
259|“……마법?”
260|
261|“주문만 영창하면 바로 발동되는 내장 마법입니다. 지속력이 꽤 길어서 앞으로 서너 시간은 문제없어요. M사에서 한정판으로 구매한 물건인데…….”
262|
263|지켜보던 임꺽정이 한마디로 축약했다.
264|
265|“엄청 비싸.”
266|
267|최 팀장의 얼굴이 살짝 어두워지는 건 기분 탓인가, 아니면 그림자 때문인가. 어쨌건 덕분에 레이드가 한결 쉬워졌다.
268|
269|‘역시 돈이 최고야.’
270|
271|세상은 자본이 지배하고 게이트도 마찬가지다. 돈 있는 놈은 마법 장비로 편하게 싸우고 없는 놈은 횃불 들어야 한다.
272|
273|“각자 위치로.”
274|
275|최 팀장의 지시에 사람들은 즉각 반응했다. 탱커 포지션인 임꺽정, 그리고 다른 E급 헌터가 선두에 섰고 최 팀장이 그다음. 짐꾼인 나와 원거리 딜러 둘이 가장 뒤에 섰다.
276|
277|“이동.”
278|
279|우리는 천천히 앞을 향해 나아가기 시작했다.
280|
281|환한 마법의 불빛이 길을 밝혀 주었다.
282|
283|“…….”
284|
285|하나 갖고 싶다.
286|
287|
288|
289|* * *
290|
291|
292|
293|“키이이잇!”
294|
295|어둠 속에 웅크리고 있던 녀석들이 괴성과 함께 모습을 드러냈다. 녹색 피부에 짧은 몸통. 흉측해 보이는 팔다리.
296|
297|일반 고블린의 상위종인 홉 고블린(Hob goblin)이다.
298|
299|‘머릿수는 대략 서른.’
300|
301|고작 다섯 명으로는 힘든 싸움이 될 것이다.
302|
303|‘하지만 C급 헌터가 있으면 이야기가 달라지지.’
304|
305|거기에 다른 네 명은 최소 십수 년 경력의 E급 베테랑.
306|
307|나는 멀찍이 물러서서 전투를 구경했다.
308|
309|“원거리!”
310|
311|최 팀장의 말이 떨어짐과 동시에 화살이 쏘아졌다. 한 발에 한 놈씩. 급소를 파고드는 화살에 방패가 없는 홉 고블린들이 우수수 쓰러진다.
312|
313|“키잇!”
314|
315|“어이고, 방패병 나왔다. 어쩔까요?”
316|
317|“대기.”
318|
319|최 팀장이 이어 말했다.
320|
321|“탱커 전진.”
322|
323|두꺼운 전신 갑옷에 타워 실드를 든 탱커들이 움직였다. 임꺽정도 그렇고, 다른 한 사람도 190센티가 넘는 거구들이라 위압감이 장난이 아니다.
324|
325|“키이이잇!”
326|
327|하지만 몬스터는 괜히 몬스터가 아니다. 머릿수만 믿은 홉 고블린들이 벌 떼처럼 달려들었다.
328|
329|하지만…….
330|
331|“어쭈.”
332|
333|뻐버벙!
334|
335|크고 아름다운 타워 실드에 피떡이 되어 날아갔다. 기세를 탄 임꺽정이 철퇴를 파리채처럼 휘두를 때마다 팔다리가 아작 나고 머리통이 박살 난다.
336|
337|“요놈! 요놈!”
338|
339|……무슨 두더지 게임이야?
340|
341|‘역시 고인물.’
342|

The official looked displeased. Understandably so. We were about to enter, yet the entire party still hadn’t arrived.

[P69]
*How much longer are we supposed to wait?*

[P70]
Only six people had gathered in front of the Gate. Excluding me, the porter, that left just five combatants.

[P71]
Since this was an E-rank Gate, we needed at least five more Hunters of the same rank… but those Peace Guild bastards were nowhere in sight. No wonder the official was annoyed.

[P72]
“You should’ve notified us in advance if you were adding personnel.”

[P73]
*Huh? What did he just say?*

[P74]
Adding personnel?

[P75]
“I’m sorry.”

[P76]
At Team Leader Choi’s curt apology, the official picked up his pen and drew several lines through the paperwork.

[P77]
“It’s not a major problem since we can amend it… but please be more careful next time.”

[P78]
“Yes.”

[P79]
*Not a major problem, my ass. We’re missing half the damn party!*

[P80]
I poked Im Kkeokjeong in the ribs.

[P81]
“Hyung. When are the others getting here?”

[P82]
“What others?”

[P83]
“The Peace Guild members.”

[P84]
“Team Leader Choi’s right there.”

[P85]
“What?”

[P86]
“Oh, did I forget to tell you? The Peace Guild is new, so it doesn’t have many people. There are only three of us, including the Guild Master. Hahaha!”

[P87]
…You’re laughing?

[P88]
“Come on, hyung.”

[P89]
“I know, punk. But you don’t need to worry.”

[P90]

[P91]
“That man’s a C-rank Hunter.”

[P92]
“Oh. C-rank…”

I shut my mouth.

[P94]
If Team Leader Choi was a C-rank Hunter, there was no problem. No, he was far better than ten E-rank Hunters. He was a mid-rank Hunter, in a completely different league from a low-rank Hunter like me.

[P95]
*I should’ve realized the moment I saw him wearing that luxury gear.*

[P96]
The man was walking around with a high-end apartment wrapped around his body. Most low-rank Hunters couldn’t afford armor like that even if they cleaned out their entire fortunes ten times over.

[P97]
A faint halo seemed to shine around Team Leader Choi’s back.

[P98]
“Please verify the signature.”

[P99]
Even the way he handed the pen back to the official looked elegant.

[P100]
Every little movement seemed to ooze wealth.

[P101]
*So this is the dignity of a C-rank Hunter.*

[P102]
*That’s fucking cool.*

[P103]
I wanted to become sworn brothers with him. To pledge brotherhood beneath the Gate—a gay oath, no, a Gate oath.

[P104]
“All right, then. Let’s go in… What is it?”

[P105]
Team Leader Choi flinched when he saw me staring.

[P106]
“Nothing. I just thought you looked cool.”

[P107]
“Excuse me?”

[P108]
“Your equipment. I said it looks cool.”

[P109]
The corner of Team Leader Choi’s mouth twitched.

[P110]
“It’s nothing special. It was merely crafted using five types of magic and B-grade Magic Gems…”

[P111]
*A nutjob I wanted to befriend.*

[P112]
* * *

[P113]
I stepped toward the Gate.

[P114]
Whoosh—

[P115]
A familiar sensation enveloped me. The cool, viscous energy unique to mana.

[P116]
Then the scenery changed.

[P117]
“It’s a cave.”

[P118]
Just as Team Leader Choi said, the raid site was a cave. The moisture-laden walls were damp, and a faint darkness shrouded our surroundings.

[P119]
“Taekyung, take out a flashlight.”

[P120]
“Yes, sir.”

[P121]
I quickly lowered my backpack. It was a porter’s bag Team Leader Choi had handed me just before we entered the Gate. It looked ordinary, but it was an expensive piece of equipment enchanted with both spatial expansion and weight reduction.

[P122]
“Here’s the flashlight.”

[P123]
I handed it over as requested, though in my experience, flashlights weren’t the best option. They were convenient, but if the light suddenly went out, your eyes wouldn’t be adjusted to the darkness.

[P124]
It was much better to wait a moment and let your eyes adjust—

[P125]
Click.

[P126]
“Let there be light. Light.”

[P127]
Whoosh. A ball of light the size of a soccer ball shot from the flashlight and plastered itself against the cave ceiling.

[P128]
“…Magic?”

[P129]
“It has a built-in spell that activates as soon as the incantation is spoken. It lasts quite a while, so it should be good for another three or four hours. It’s a limited-edition item I purchased from Company M…”

[P130]
Im Kkeokjeong summed it up in three words.

[P131]
“It’s crazy expensive.”

[P132]
Was it my imagination, or had Team Leader Choi’s face darkened slightly? Maybe it was just the shadows.

[P133]
Either way, the raid had become much easier thanks to him.

[P134]
*Money really is the best.*

[P135]
Capital ruled the world, and Gates were no exception. People with money fought in comfort using enchanted equipment. People without it carried torches.

[P136]
“Take your positions.”

[P137]
Everyone responded immediately to Team Leader Choi’s command. Im Kkeokjeong and the other E-rank tank took the lead, with Team Leader Choi behind them. I stood at the very back with the two ranged dealers.

[P138]
“Move.”

[P139]
We began advancing slowly.

[P140]
The bright magical light illuminated the path ahead.

[P141]
“…”

[P142]
*I want one.*

[P143]
* * *

[P144]
“Kiiiieet!”

[P145]
The creatures crouching in the darkness emerged with shrill cries. Green skin, squat bodies, and grotesque limbs.

[P146]
They were Hobgoblins, an evolved form of ordinary goblin.

[P147]
*About thirty of them.*

[P148]
With only five combatants, this would be a difficult fight.

[P149]
*But having a C-rank Hunter changes everything.*

[P150]
Besides, the other four were veteran E-rank Hunters with at least a decade of experience each.

[P151]
I hung well back and watched the battle.

[P152]
“Ranged!”

[P153]
Arrows flew the instant Team Leader Choi gave the order.

[P154]
One shot, one kill.

[P155]
The arrows buried themselves in vital points, dropping the unshielded Hobgoblins one after another.

[P156]
“Kiit!”

[P157]
“Oh, look. Shield-bearers. What do we do?”

[P158]
“Hold.”

[P159]
Team Leader Choi issued his next command.

[P160]
“Tanks, advance.”

[P161]
The tanks moved forward in thick full-body armor, tower shields raised. Im Kkeokjeong and the other man were both hulking giants over 190 centimeters tall. The sight of them alone was intimidating.

[P162]
“Kiiiieet!”

[P163]
But monsters were called monsters for a reason. Trusting in their superior numbers, the Hobgoblins swarmed forward like bees.

[P164]
But—

[P165]
“Well, look at you.”

[P166]
Bam!

[P167]
They smashed into the big, beautiful tower shields and flew back as bloody pulp. Seizing the momentum, Im Kkeokjeong swung his mace like a flyswatter, shattering limbs and crushing skulls with every blow.

[P168]
“Got you! And you!”

[P169]
…What was this, whack-a-mole?

[P170]
*Veterans, all right.*

[P171]
All four of them stayed within their roles without overextending themselves, steadily whittling down the enemy numbers.

[P172]
Knowing when to fall back and when to advance was the kind of combat sense that came only from extensive experience.

[P173]
“Everyone, hold your positions.”

[P174]
Then the last man moved.

[P175]
The one who had been directing the flow of battle until now.

[P176]
“I’ll take care of the rest.”

[P177]
A red streak flashed across his armor as he plunged into the twenty remaining Hobgoblins.

[P178]
Slash—

[P179]
A head soared into the air along a clean arc. It happened so quickly that the monsters couldn’t even react.

[P180]
“Kiiie?”

[P181]
Slash. Slash. Slash.

[P182]
The blade never stopped. Merciless and efficient, it pierced and severed one vital point after another.

[P183]
This was no longer a battle.

[P184]
It was a massacre—one man slaughtering more than twenty monsters.

[P185]
*So this is a C-rank Hunter.*

[P186]
His speed. His strength.

[P187]
I could see it all. And I could feel it.

[P188]
*He really is strong.*

[P189]
As a mere F-rank, I couldn’t even dream of matching him. He was a mid-rank Hunter, three full ranks above me. A broad river and a towering wall that effort alone could never overcome.

[P190]
Yet at the same time, a question arose.

[P191]
*What if this were Murim?*

[P192]
Team Leader Choi was unquestionably strong. He had the abilities befitting a C-rank Hunter and plenty of experience.

[P193]
But if this were Murim… if he were a martial artist…

[P194]
*I’d be stronger.*

[P195]
His movements were fast and powerful, but that was all. He hadn’t learned martial arts, nor did he use his mana efficiently.

[P196]
At best, he was First Rate. In Murim, that was exactly where he would stand.

[P197]
*But this is reality.*

[P198]
I bit my lip without realizing it.

[P199]
A mid-rank Hunter and a bottom-rank Hunter.

[P200]
While the mid-rank Hunter wore expensive equipment and slaughtered monsters, the bottom-rank Hunter could only stand and watch.

[P201]
As a porter.

[P202]
“Kiiieet…”

[P203]
The last Hobgoblin fell. Team Leader Choi pulled his sword from its chest, and our eyes met.

[P204]
“Taekyung, please take care of the byproducts.”

[P205]
“…”

[P206]
“Taekyung?”

[P207]
I wanted to tell him that I was stronger than him.

[P208]
But in the end, I couldn’t. Because this was my reality.

[P209]
“…Thank you for your hard work.”

[P210]
I *used to be* stronger than you.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

“That’s Gate officials for you. There’s a reason everyone calls this a cushy posting.”

[P19]
*It’s been a while.*

[P20]
The way it fit snugly in my hand felt both familiar and strange.

[P21]
It was definitely different from the weapon I’d used for the past month… No. Never mind. I shouldn’t think about that anymore.

[P22]
*I need to forget all of it.*

[P23]

[P24]

[P25]
“All ready?”

[P26]
“Yeah. Pretty much.”

[P27]

[P28]

[P29]

[P30]

[P31]
1.98 million won.

[P32]
*I could barely sleep for days after buying it.*

[P33]
Being a Hunter cost about as much as it paid, and most of those expenses went toward equipment. It was all because of the unique nature of Gates.

[P34]
*Equipment that isn’t imbued with mana or magic breaks down in no time.*

That was why most gear was crafted using Magic Gems obtained from Gate monsters.

[P36]
The higher the Grade of the Magic Gem, the more the price shot through the roof.

“Seven years? Good grief. Saving money is all well and good, but you’ve got to spend it when it counts. You really want to pinch pennies when your life’s on the line?”

[P38]
“Hmm. I had my reasons.”

“You’re in a noncombat position today, so you should be fine… but be careful.”

“I will.”

[P43]

“Is everyone ready?”

[P46]
*No way.*

“Is that a Red Drake leather set?”

[P48]
“Hmm.”

[P49]

[P50]
“Ah, sorry…”

“It’s nothing special. It was merely crafted using five types of magic and B-grade Magic Gems.”

[P52]
“…”

[P53]

[P54]
“Ah. Right.”

[P55]
“Red Drake leather is popular for its distinctive sheen, but it only looks impressive. It isn’t particularly useful.”

[P56]
Team Leader Choi shifted his stiff posture, and a faint red light shimmered across the armor.

[P57]
“But it is exceptionally beautiful.”

[P58]
“…”

[P59]
“Let’s head downstairs.”

[P60]
Team Leader Choi left the waiting room first. Im Kkeokjeong sidled over to me.

[P61]
“That guy loves it when someone recognizes his equipment.”

[P62]
“I mean, I get that, but… what’s with him?”

[P63]
“No idea. He’s an equipment nut. There’s even a rumor that he blew his entire fortune on that set and sleeps in it every night.”

[P64]
*So that bastard’s a nutjob too.*

[P65]
I sighed inwardly and prayed that today’s raid would end without incident.

[P68]

[P69]
*How much longer are we supposed to wait?*

[P70]

[P72]
“You should’ve notified us in advance if you were adding personnel.”

[P74]
Adding personnel?

[P75]
“I’m sorry.”

[P76]

“It’s not a major problem since we can amend it… but please be more careful next time.”

“Yes.”

[P80]

“Come on, hyung.”

“That man’s a C-rank Hunter.”

[P95]
*I should’ve realized the moment I saw him wearing that luxury gear.*

[P96]
The man was walking around with a high-end apartment wrapped around his body. Most low-rank Hunters couldn’t afford armor like that even if they cleaned out their entire fortunes ten times over.

[P97]
A faint halo seemed to shine around Team Leader Choi’s back.

[P98]
“Please verify the signature.”

[P99]
Even the way he handed the pen back to the official looked elegant.

[P100]
Every little movement seemed to ooze wealth.

[P101]
*So this is the dignity of a C-rank Hunter.*

[P102]
*That’s fucking cool.*

[P103]
I wanted to become sworn brothers with him. To pledge brotherhood beneath the Gate—a gay oath, no, a Gate oath.

[P104]
“All right, then. Let’s go in… What is it?”

[P105]
Team Leader Choi flinched when he saw me staring.

[P106]
“Nothing. I just thought you looked cool.”

[P107]
“Excuse me?”

[P108]
“Your equipment. I said it looks cool.”

[P109]
The corner of Team Leader Choi’s mouth twitched.

[P110]
“It’s nothing special. It was merely crafted using five types of magic and B-grade Magic Gems…”

[P111]
*A nutjob I wanted to befriend.*

[P112]

[P113]
I stepped toward the Gate.

[P114]
Whoosh—

[P115]
A familiar sensation enveloped me. The cool, viscous energy unique to mana.

[P116]
Then the scenery changed.

[P117]
“It’s a cave.”

[P118]
Just as Team Leader Choi said, the raid site was a cave. The moisture-laden walls were damp, and a faint darkness shrouded our surroundings.

[P119]
“Taekyung, take out a flashlight.”

[P120]
“Yes, sir.”

[P121]
I quickly lowered my backpack. It was a porter’s bag Team Leader Choi had handed me just before we entered the Gate. It looked ordinary, but it was an expensive piece of equipment enchanted with both spatial expansion and weight reduction.

[P122]
“Here’s the flashlight.”

[P123]
I handed it over as requested, though in my experience, flashlights weren’t the best option. They were convenient, but if the light suddenly went out, your eyes wouldn’t be adjusted to the darkness.

[P124]
It was much better to wait a moment and let your eyes adjust—

[P125]
Click.

[P126]
“Let there be light. Light.”

[P127]
Whoosh. A ball of light the size of a soccer ball shot from the flashlight and plastered itself against the cave ceiling.

[P128]
“…Magic?”

[P129]
“It has a built-in spell that activates as soon as the incantation is spoken. It lasts quite a while, so it should be good for another three or four hours. It’s a limited-edition item I purchased from Company M…”

[P130]
Im Kkeokjeong summed it up in three words.

[P131]
“It’s crazy expensive.”

[P132]
Was it my imagination, or had Team Leader Choi’s face darkened slightly? Maybe it was just the shadows.

[P133]
Either way, the raid had become much easier thanks to him.

[P134]
*Money really is the best.*

[P135]
Capital ruled the world, and Gates were no exception. People with money fought in comfort using enchanted equipment. People without it carried torches.

[P136]
“Take your positions.”

[P137]
Everyone responded immediately to Team Leader Choi’s command. Im Kkeokjeong and the other E-rank tank took the lead, with Team Leader Choi behind them. I stood at the very back with the two ranged dealers.

[P138]
“Move.”

[P139]
We began advancing slowly.

[P140]
The bright magical light illuminated the path ahead.

[P141]
“…”

[P142]
*I want one.*

[P143]
* * *

[P144]
“Kiiiieet!”

[P145]
The creatures crouching in the darkness emerged with shrill cries. Green skin, squat bodies, and grotesque limbs.

[P146]
They were Hobgoblins, an evolved form of ordinary goblin.

[P147]
*About thirty of them.*

[P148]
With only five combatants, this would be a difficult fight.

[P149]
*But having a C-rank Hunter changes everything.*

[P150]
Besides, the other four were veteran E-rank Hunters with at least a decade of experience each.

[P151]
I hung well back and watched the battle.

[P152]
“Ranged!”

[P153]
Arrows flew the instant Team Leader Choi gave the order.

[P154]
One shot, one kill.

[P155]
The arrows buried themselves in vital points, dropping the unshielded Hobgoblins one after another.

[P156]
“Kiit!”

[P157]
“Oh, look. Shield-bearers. What do we do?”

[P158]
“Hold.”

[P159]
Team Leader Choi issued his next command.

[P160]
“Tanks, advance.”

[P161]
The tanks moved forward in thick full-body armor, tower shields raised. Im Kkeokjeong and the other man were both hulking giants over 190 centimeters tall. The sight of them alone was intimidating.

[P162]
“Kiiiieet!”

[P163]
But monsters were called monsters for a reason. Trusting in their superior numbers, the Hobgoblins swarmed forward like bees.

[P164]
But—

[P165]
“Well, look at you.”

[P166]
Bam!

[P167]
They smashed into the big, beautiful tower shields and flew back as bloody pulp. Seizing the momentum, Im Kkeokjeong swung his mace like a flyswatter, shattering limbs and crushing skulls with every blow.

[P168]
“Got you! And you!”

[P169]
…What was this, whack-a-mole?

[P170]
*Veterans, all right.*

[P171]
All four of them stayed within their roles without overextending themselves, steadily whittling down the enemy numbers.

[P172]
Knowing when to fall back and when to advance was the kind of combat sense that came only from extensive experience.

[P173]
“Everyone, hold your positions.”

[P174]
Then the last man moved.

[P175]
The one who had been directing the flow of battle until now.

[P176]
“I’ll take care of the rest.”

[P177]
A red streak flashed across his armor as he plunged into the twenty remaining Hobgoblins.

[P178]
Slash—

[P179]
A head soared into the air along a clean arc. It happened so quickly that the monsters couldn’t even react.

[P180]
“Kiiie?”

[P181]
Slash. Slash. Slash.

[P182]
The blade never stopped. Merciless and efficient, it pierced and severed one vital point after another.

[P183]
This was no longer a battle.

[P184]
It was a massacre—one man slaughtering more than twenty monsters.

[P185]
*So this is a C-rank Hunter.*

[P186]
His speed. His strength.

[P187]
I could see it all. And I could feel it.

[P188]
*He really is strong.*

[P189]
As a mere F-rank, I couldn’t even dream of matching him. He was a mid-rank Hunter, three full ranks above me. A broad river and a towering wall that effort alone could never overcome.

[P190]
Yet at the same time, a question arose.

[P191]
*What if this were Murim?*

[P192]
Team Leader Choi was unquestionably strong. He had the abilities befitting a C-rank Hunter and plenty of experience.

[P193]
But if this were Murim… if he were a martial artist…

[P194]
*I’d be stronger.*

[P195]
His movements were fast and powerful, but that was all. He hadn’t learned martial arts, nor did he use his mana efficiently.

[P196]
At best, he was First Rate. In Murim, that was exactly where he would stand.

[P197]
*But this is reality.*

[P198]
I bit my lip without realizing it.

[P199]
A mid-rank Hunter and a bottom-rank Hunter.

[P200]
While the mid-rank Hunter wore expensive equipment and slaughtered monsters, the bottom-rank Hunter could only stand and watch.

[P201]
As a porter.

[P202]
“Kiiieet…”

[P203]
The last Hobgoblin fell. Team Leader Choi pulled his sword from its chest, and our eyes met.

[P204]
“Taekyung, please take care of the byproducts.”

[P205]
“…”

[P206]
“Taekyung?”

[P207]
I wanted to tell him that I was stronger than him.

[P208]
But in the end, I couldn’t. Because this was my reality.

[P209]
“…Thank you for your hard work.”

[P210]
I *used to be* stronger than you.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.

- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 42

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃42화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|게이트(Gate).
  6|
  7|대격변이 남긴 가장 큰 흔적.
  8|
  9|삼십여 년 전 마왕 아스모데우스가 침략 루트로 사용했던 그곳은, 헌터들의 생계 수단이자 마정석이라는 고차원 에너지 자원의 발굴 현장으로 전락한 지 오래였다.
 10|
 11|“평화 길드 분들이시죠?”
 12|
 13|입구에 나와 있던 작업복 차림의 중년인이 다가왔다.
 14|
 15|게이트마다 배치된 게이트 관리청 소속의 공무원이다.
 16|
 17|“네.”
 18|
 19|최 팀장의 무뚝뚝한 대답에 공무원이 고개를 끄덕였다.
 20|
 21|“딱 맞춰 오셨네요. 언제 진입하실 겁니까?”
 22|
 23|“장비 갖추고 바로 들어가겠습니다.”
 24|
 25|“2층에 대기실 있으니까 준비 마치고 내려오시면 됩니다. 그럼.”
 26|
 27|우리는 최 팀장을 따라 이동했다. 관리청 공무원이 상주하는 2층짜리 건물은 낡을 대로 낡았는데, 대기실 역시 비슷한 상황이었다.
 28|
 29|‘와 씨. 냄새 봐라.’
 30|
 31|문을 열자마자 땀 냄새가 코를 찌른다. 녹슨 캐비닛과 꽉 찬 휴지통도 눈에 띄었다.
 32|
 33|“여긴 좀 심하네. 환기도 안 시키나?”
 34|
 35|“게이트 담당 공무원들이 그렇지 뭐. 괜히 꿀 보직이 아니여.”
 36|
 37|나는 투덜거리는 소리를 뒤로하고 레이드 장비로 환복하기 시작했다. 가죽 갑옷에 가벼운 소재의 전투화. 마지막으로 길쭉한 케이스에서 창을 꺼내 쥐었다.
 38|
 39|‘오랜만이네.’
 40|
 41|손아귀에 딱 들어오는 이 감촉. 익숙하면서도 낯설다.
 42|
 43|지난 한 달 동안 썼던 무기와는 확실히 차이가…… 아, 아니다. 더는 생각하지 말자.
 44|
 45|‘이젠 다 잊어야지.’
 46|
 47|괜히 멀쩡한 전투화 끈을 조이는 내게 임꺽정이 다가왔다.
 48|
 49|그는 전신 갑옷과 거대한 타워 실드를 갖춘 메인 탱커의 모습이었다.
 50|
 51|“준비 끝났어?”
 52|
 53|“예. 뭐.”
 54|
 55|나를 위아래로 훑어본 임꺽정이 혀를 내둘렀다.
 56|
 57|“이 녀석 보게. 도대체 언제 적 장비야?”
 58|
 59|“글쎄요. 처음 시작할 때 샀으니까 적어도 7년?”
 60|
 61|초짜 시절, 동대문 지하 매장에서 큰맘 먹고 질렀더랬다. 가격도 정확히 기억한다. 198만 원.
 62|
 63|‘지르고 나서 며칠 동안 잠도 제대로 못 잤지.’
 64|
 65|헌터는 수입만큼 지출도 큰 직업이다. 그 지출의 대부분을 차지하는 게 장비 관련이고. 이게 다 게이트의 특수성 때문이다.
 66|
 67|‘마나, 혹은 마력이 깃들지 않은 장비는 금방 망가지니까.’
 68|
 69|그래서 가장 흔하게 쓰이는 방법이 게이트 몬스터에게 얻은 마정석을 재료로 장비를 제작하는 거다.
 70|
 71|사용된 마정석의 등급이 높을수록 가격은 천정부지로 솟는다.
 72|
 73|“7년? 세상에. 아무리 돈이 좋아도 쓸 때는 써야지. 목숨에 돈 아낄래?”
 74|
 75|“음. 사정이 있었어요.”
 76|
 77|굳이 말하고 싶지 않은 사정이다. 임꺽정은 걱정스러운 목소리로 말했다.
 78|
 79|“오늘은 비전투 포지션이니 괜찮겠지만…… 조심해라.”
 80|
 81|“네.”
 82|
 83|대답하면서도 기분이 묘하다. 얼마 전까지 조심하라는 말을 입에 달고 살던 누군가가 떠올라서.
 84|
 85|하지만 감상에 젖는 것도 잠시.
 86|
 87|“다들 준비 끝나셨습니까?”
 88|
 89|최 팀장의 등장에 나는 입을 딱 벌렸다.
 90|
 91|저거 설마.
 92|
 93|“붉은 드레이크 가죽 세트?”
 94|
 95|“음.”
 96|
 97|최 팀장의 얼굴이 굳었다. 명품관 카탈로그에서나 보던 거라 나도 모르게 그만 실수했다.
 98|
 99|“아, 죄송합…….”
100|
101|“별거 아닙니다. 다섯 종류의 마법과 B급 마정석을 재료로 만들었을 뿐이죠.”
102|
103|“……?”
104|
105|“강조하는 건 아니지만 다섯 종류의 마법과 B급 마정석이 재료입니다.”
106|
107|“아, 네.”
108|
109|“붉은 드레이크의 가죽이 인기가 좋은 건 특유의 윤기 때문인데, 보기에만 그럴듯하고 별 쓸모는 없습니다.”
110|
111|최 팀장이 굳은 얼굴로 몸을 움직였다. 은은한 붉은 빛이 번뜩였다.
112|
113|“하지만 매우 아름답죠.”
114|
115|“…….”
116|
117|“이만 내려갑시다.”
118|
119|최 팀장이 먼저 대기실을 나가자 임꺽정이 다가와 말했다.
120|
121|“저 친구 장비 알아봐 주는 거 엄청 좋아해.”
122|
123|“아니 뭐, 이해는 가는데…… 왜 저래요?”
124|
125|“몰라. 장비 덕후야. 전 재산 털어서 저거 사고 밤마다 입고 잔다는 소문도 있어.”
126|
127|저 자식도 또라이구나.
128|
129|나는 내심 한탄하며 오늘 레이드가 무사히 끝나길 빌었다.
130|
131|
132|
133|* * *
134|
135|
136|
137|“신청하신 인원이랑 다르군요.”
138|
139|공무원은 불편한 표정이었다. 그럴 만도 하지. 이제 진입해야 하는데 인원이 전부 안 모였으니까.
140|
141|‘도대체 얼마나 기다려야 하나.’
142|
143|현재 게이트 앞에 집결한 인원은 여섯 명. 짐꾼으로 온 나를 제외하면 전투 인원은 다섯밖에 안 된다.
144|
145|E급 게이트니까 최소한 동급의 헌터 다섯이 더 필요한데…… 평화 길드 놈들이 코빼기도 보이지 않으니 공무원 입장에서는 짜증이 날 수밖에.
146|
147|“추가된 인원이 있으면 미리 말씀을 해 주셔야죠.”
148|
149|응? 방금 뭐라고 한 거냐.
150|
151|추가된 인원이라니?
152|
153|“죄송합니다.”
154|
155|최 팀장의 무뚝뚝한 사과에 공무원이 펜을 들어 서류에 좍좍 줄을 그었다.
156|
157|“뭐 수정하면 되니까 큰 문제는 없는데…… 다음부턴 조심해 주십쇼.”
158|
159|“예.”
160|
161|큰 문제가 없기는 시발. 사람이 없잖아, 사람이!
162|
163|나는 임꺽정의 옆구리를 쿡 찔렀다.
164|
165|“형님. 다른 사람들은 언제 와요?”
166|
167|“무슨 사람들?”
168|
169|“평화 길드요.”
170|
171|“최 팀장 있잖아.”
172|
173|“네?”
174|
175|“아, 말 안 했었나? 평화 길드, 신생이라 인원이 없어. 길드장 포함 세 명이 전부지. 으하하.”
176|
177|……웃어?
178|
179|“아니, 형님.”
180|
181|“알아, 인마. 근데 걱정 안 해도 돼.”
182|
183|내 어깨를 툭 친 임꺽정이 서류에 사인 중인 최 팀장을 가리켰다.
184|
185|“저 양반, C급 헌터거든.”
186|
187|“아. C급…….”
188|
189|나는 입을 다물었다. 최 팀장이 C급 헌터라면 문제없다. 아니, E급 헌터 열 명보다 훨씬 낫다. 그는 나 같은 하급 헌터와 격이 다른 ‘중급 헌터’니까.
190|
191|‘명품 장비 걸쳤을 때부터 알아차렸어야 했는데.’
192|
193|고급 아파트를 몸에 두르고 다니는 인간이다. 어지간한 하급 헌터들은 전 재산을 열 번 털어도 못 사는 가격.
194|
195|최 팀장의 뒷모습에서 은은한 후광이 비쳤다.
196|
197|“서명 확인 바랍니다.”
198|
199|공무원에게 펜을 넘겨주는 모습도 어쩜 저렇게 우아하냐.
200|
201|작은 움직임조차 부티가 좔좔 흐르는 것 같다.
202|
203|저게 바로 C급 헌터의 품격인가.
204|
205|‘존나 멋있어.’
206|
207|의형제 맺고 싶다. 게이트 아래에서 게이결의, 아니 게이트결의 맺고 싶다.
208|

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
